evidence.description: The response metadata is discarded, and the body is decoded without checking whether the HTTP request succeeded.
Decoded results are used to update stored statistics.

candidates.explanation: URLSession does not throw merely because an HTTP response has an error status. Consequently, this method can accept an unsuccessful response as a successful update if its body matches the expected schema; otherwise, the HTTP failure is obscured by a decoding error.
candidates.title: HTTP response status is ignored

evidence.description: The singleton exposes mutable statistics without actor isolation or synchronization.
A public asynchronous method writes the shared properties, including related value and timestamp fields in separate assignments.

candidates.explanation: Concurrent callers can access the same Statistics instance while fetchAndUpdate mutates its properties. No visible isolation protects reads or writes, allowing data races and observations of partially updated state, including mismatched values and timestamps.
candidates.title: Shared mutable statistics lack concurrency isolation

evidence.description: The date formatter is configured exclusively with the fractional-seconds option.
Both the trees-planted value and its timestamp are skipped when date parsing fails.
Total-investment updates are also conditional on successful date parsing.

candidates.explanation: This formatter configuration requires fractional seconds, excluding otherwise valid ISO 8601 internet timestamps that omit them. Such a timestamp causes the corresponding numeric statistic to remain unchanged as well, and fetchAndUpdate completes without reporting that the update was discarded.
candidates.title: Date parsing excludes ISO 8601 timestamps without fractional seconds
